newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela may fund labour reform with Orimulsion.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela may fund labour reform with Orimulsion.

text.p: Venezuela is considering using future Orimulsion sales to back debt issues with which it will liquidate its old severance pay system, Finance Minister Luis Matos said on Tuesday.
Venezuela had originally ear-marked Orimulsion sales for a special account called the Debt Rescue Fund that would be used to pay down foreign debt.

"The debt rescue fund could issue paper backed by sales of Orimulsion or bitumen to pay these (severance pay) debts," Matos told deputies attending a congressional commission studying planned labour law and social security reforms.

Matos said the total cost spread over five years of liquidating the old system would amount to $8.7 billion. Total Orimulsion sales in 1996 generated 73 billion bolivars ($153 million) on 4.5 milliion tonnes.

Orimulsion is a new boiler fuel unique to Venezuela which competes with coal in world markets. Matos said that revenues from these exports could be used because they are not included in the annual budget, but that this was only one possible means of financing.
Under labour law reforms currently under dicussion in Congress, Venezuela would pay its 1.2 million public sector workers an initial 25 percent of the total debt.
